Steps.Say: They're fussy about the nesting boxes. One likes the corner, one likes the middle, and one acts like the whole coop is reserved.
I can tell them apart by the way they walk. Don't ask me to explain it. I just can.
Jas named the smallest one Pickle. The chicken is not a pickle. I stopped arguing because it was getting me nowhere.
She's been drawing more lately. I put the pictures on the wall. Some of them are upside down, but that feels intentional.
She asked if grown-ups ever get scared of the dark. I told her yes. She said, 'Then keep the lamp on.' Fair enough.
I don't always know what to say to her. So I try to show up, and I try not to pretend I know everything.
Marnie knows every animal's habits, injuries, and preferred breakfast. She says it's not difficult. She's lying about that last part.
She can tell when I'm avoiding a conversation by the way I stack the feed bags. Apparently I have a very obvious system.
She deserves a day off that doesn't involve somebody calling about a missing cow. I've been trying to cover the morning chores.
Gus keeps the lights warm and the questions optional. That's why I still go sometimes.
Pam tells the same story about the bus every week. I know all the pauses now. I still laugh at the wrong bit.
I'm trying to decide that leaving early is allowed. It turns out the door works both ways.
The warehouse smelled like cardboard and floor cleaner. The clock was louder than the people.
I learned to look busy when there wasn't anything to do. I still catch myself doing it in the barn.
I don't miss the place. I miss knowing exactly when my shift ended. That's a different thing.
Pepper poppers are good when somebody else makes them. Mine come out like a dare.
I put too much salt in the soup yesterday. Marnie said it was fine. She drank three glasses of water afterward.
If you bring me a recipe, I'll try it. Don't expect a review. I'll give you a grunt and a thumbs-up.
The nights are better when I don't take the whole day to bed with me. Not a perfect system, but a start.
I leave the window cracked when it rains. The sound covers the clock. The clock's a real nuisance.
Some mornings I wake up before the alarm and don't immediately start counting what went wrong. That's new.
People here notice when a fence is broken. Sometimes they notice before the person who owns the fence.
The bus stop looks different now that it's running again. I still remember when it was just a place to stand and wait.
You made the old farm feel busy again. Even from the ranch, we can hear the shipping bin lid.
I like having a room to myself. I don't like feeling like I need an excuse to use it.
The difference is probably obvious to everybody else. It took me a while.
You don't have to fill every silence. Sometimes you can just sit there and let the kettle finish.
I'm not making a five-year plan. I don't even trust a five-day plan yet.
I know what I want tomorrow to look like. Feed the chickens, fix the small fence, eat something decent.
That's enough for now. Maybe later I'll want something bigger. I'm trying not to rush it.
Don't buy me something because you think I need cheering up. If you see something I'd actually use, that's different.
A good coffee mug is a serious purchase. It has to fit the hand and not wobble on the table.
Jas made me a bracelet out of string. It's too small for my wrist, so I tied it around the thermos.
Your animals are loud in the morning. That's not a complaint. It's a pretty good sound to wake up to.
I can help carry feed if you get a delivery. I won't promise to smile while doing it.
The first time I visited, I thought the farm would swallow you whole. Looks like you taught it some manners.
Marnie says I should take a day off. I said I would. Now I'm staring at the calendar like it's a trap.

Options.Label: Tell her you'll take Sunday and mean it.

Steps.Say: Sunday. No excuses. If I start inventing chores, you can take the screwdriver away.

Options.Label: Ask what she'd do with a free day.

Steps.Say: Probably sleep. Maybe walk. ...I could do that. I don't need a full itinerary.

Options.Label: Offer to cover the morning chores.

Steps.Say: That'd help. Don't make a big thing of it. I'll owe you a quiet breakfast.
I found an old photo from Joja. Everyone looks exhausted. I look like I was trying to disappear.

Options.Label: You look like you were getting through it.

Steps.Say: Yeah. That's what it was. Getting through it. Doesn't mean I want to go back.

Options.Label: Keep it as a reminder of how far you've come.

Steps.Say: Maybe. I'll put it in a drawer, not on the wall. That's as sentimental as I get.

Options.Label: Throw it away if you don't want it.

Steps.Say: I might. Not today, though. I want to decide when I'm not annoyed.
Jas wants to enter a drawing in the fair. She's worried the other kids will laugh.

Options.Label: Tell her you'll stand with her.

Steps.Say: I'll be there. She can look over and see me making a face at anyone who laughs.

Options.Label: Help her practise showing it to people.

Steps.Say: Good idea. We can put it on the feed shed first. The chickens are a harsh audience.

Options.Label: Remind her she likes making things.

Steps.Say: That's what I'll say. Then I'll help her find the blue pencil she lost. Again.
The saloon was full last night. I left before it got too loud. Pam said she'd save my seat.
Yeah. She doesn't make a speech about it. Just saves the seat. I appreciate that.

Options.Label: Maybe you can invite someone next time.

Steps.Say: Maybe. One person. Two at most. Don't turn it into an event.

Options.Label: You can leave whenever you want.

Steps.Say: I know. I'm practising remembering that when the room gets noisy.

Steps.Narrate: You find a quiet place with Shane. Nobody is in a hurry to leave.
Rain keeps the chickens under the eaves. Shane shares the dry patch with you and pretends she isn't making room.

Steps.Say: It's a decent place to sit. The roof leaks over there, though. Don't get attached to that corner.

Steps.Narrate: The two of you sort a basket of eggs. Shane checks each shell twice, then lets you handle the easy ones.

Steps.Say: You have a gentle touch. Don't tell the chickens. They'll start expecting professional service.

Steps.Narrate: At sunset, Shane brings two mugs out to the coop. One has a chipped handle, but she uses it anyway.

Steps.Say: I kept the good one for you. Don't ask why. I just did.

Steps.Narrate: You walk the ranch fence and stop where the grass meets the forest path. A chicken follows for three steps, then gives up.

Steps.Say: She'll come back. They always do. ...I think that's why I like this place.

Children.Label: Remember the first visit?
Children.Say: The latch finally stayed shut. I still check it when the wind picks up. Habit. At least this one's useful.

Children.Label: Remember what we decided?
Children.Say: That morning with the thermos? I washed it before bed. Small thing, but I remembered to do it.

Children.Label: Remember that afternoon?
Children.Say: The coop sign is still crooked. Jas says it gives the place character. I'm not arguing with her.
